studies.label: Laboratory team press-release experiment: unequal versus full AI access, with a common no-AI baseline
studies.cluster_se_treatment: The unadjusted treatment-phase comparisons use one press-release score or one teammate-pair distance per randomized team. The OLS model uses repeated team-task submissions from both phases and does not report clustering by team. The article does not specify a cluster-robust variance estimator. Mediation-model observation counts and repeated-team handling are not reconciled with the OLS sample.

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 6, Sections 3 and 3.1 (reported experimental people count and randomized teams); PDF p. 11, Table 3, condition headers (team counts); PDF p. 10, Section 4.4.1 (Table 3 describes team-level baseline observations).
counts_source.quote:
This experiment involved 120 participants, who were made up of undergraduates and graduate students from a university in China.

arms.name: Unequal AI access
arms.description: In the treatment-phase AR-glasses press-release task, only one randomly selected member of each two-person team could use Kimi without restrictions on interaction. This is condition 1 (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2). Table 3 prints the corresponding baseline team count; arm-level people counts are not printed.

arms.name: Full AI access
arms.description: Both members could use Kimi for the treatment-phase AR-glasses press-release task. This is condition 2 (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2). Table 3 prints the corresponding baseline team count; arm-level people counts are not printed.

arms.name: No AI access (earlier common baseline)
arms.description: Every team first wrote an electric-bicycle press release without GenAI. This is a repeated baseline phase of the same sample, not a separately randomized arm. The order and product prompt were fixed, so its comparisons with the later AI task are excluded (PDF p. 6, Sections 3.2–3.3; PDF p. 14, Section 5.4).

studies.task: Two-person teams collaboratively wrote a 700-character Chinese press release about an electric bicycle without AI and then about AR glasses with their assigned AI access; each task was limited to 45 minutes (PDF p. 6, Section 3.3).

ai_tool.name: Kimi 3.0 (Moonshot), as named by the paper
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 6, Sections 3 and 3.2; the tool release year is not stated.

studies.shared_sample: The screening form reports overlap as not_stated and identifies DOI 10.1002/pra2.1437 as an unresolved possible shared-sample report. The citation record later identifies that proceedings report as likely the same work from matching authors, experiment, and findings, but states that formal version linkage is unconfirmed. The source journal PDF supplies no sample-linkage statement; neither confirmed independence nor an additional independent sample is assumed.

estimates.outcome: Task quality: overall expert grade (unadjusted comparison)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Overall grade (1–7) assigned by blinded marketing experts based on writing quality, content quality, and originality. Each submission was evaluated by multiple independent raters; the main article does not explicitly state how the ratings were combined into the submission grade (PDF pp. 6–7, Section 3.4.2.1).

Evaluators assigned an overall grade (1–7) to the writing task submissions based on three criteria: writing quality, content quality, and originality.

estimates.notes: The eligible contrast compares the two randomized AI configurations during the treatment-phase task. Each scored press release is a team output, so the unadjusted between-team comparison has one output per randomized team; se_basis is cluster on that basis. The article does not print the test degrees of freedom or an analysis-specific observation or people count. The dispersions are explicitly labeled SD in the prose and are transcribed into the SD fields without conversion. Figure 4 on PDF p. 9 instead says its error bars are standard errors of the mean. The SD/SE discrepancy is unresolved: these values should not be treated as confirmed standardizers. The numeric fields preserve values; the source quotes preserve printed trailing zeros. No mean difference, confidence interval, or standardized effect is printed for this contrast. Quality is coded usefulness because the outcome is an overall task-quality grade including originality, rather than an explicitly named creativity rating. It is quality of a creative product press release, not an expository-writing proficiency test.

regression.model: OLS, Table 1 Model (1). Regresses task quality on indicators for no access and full access, with unequal access as the reference, controlling for female proportion, team problem-solving ability, team creativity, and marketing experience. These covariates were measured before treatment (PDF pp. 6 and 8). The coefficient is full minus unequal access, or control minus treatment in this record; its printed sign is retained.

estimates.notes: This is a second analysis of the same task-quality outcome and randomized AI-arm contrast, not an independent study or sample. Arm means and dispersions are in the separate unadjusted record; the regression does not print adjusted arm means. The coefficient and t statistic are copied with their negative signs: the paper models full access relative to unequal access, whereas the extraction names unequal access as treatment. No sign reversal has been calculated. The adjacent column is headed SD but contains negative entries; the footnote calls them t statistics. The adjacent value is therefore retained as the paper-labeled t statistic, with its labeling conflict flagged, and the regression SE remains null. The model N is a count of team-task submissions from the common baseline and AI phase, not a count of independent people or randomized teams. Team clustering or team random effects are not reported, so se_basis is output. No analysis-specific people counts are printed. The common no-AI baseline coefficient is excluded as nonrandomized.

estimates.outcome: Cognitive diversity between teammates’ spoken contributions (unadjusted comparison)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Cosine distance between the two teammates’ concatenated spoken contributions over the entire task discussion. Audio was transcribed and manually corrected; each member’s text was encoded with the Universal Sentence Encoder from TensorFlow Hub and normalized to unit length. The measure compares different people within each team, not final press releases across teams. Higher distance means greater diversity. No embedding-model version is specified (PDF p. 7, Section 3.4.3).

sources.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 4.2, independent-sample comparison of unequal and full AI access
sources.quote: unequal AI access exhibited significantly higher cognitive diversity (M = 0.631, SD = 0.011) than those with full AI access (M = 0.510, SD = 0.018), t = 5.938, p < 0.01.

estimates.notes: Each team contributes one cosine distance between the pair of member-level text outputs. Thus unit is team, sd_level is pair (one pair per team), and the unadjusted independent-sample t test compares randomized team clusters. The measure is within-team, between-person diversity, not within-person flexibility and not similarity of the final written products across teams. The article prints no analysis-specific count or degrees of freedom for this t test. The arm levels and paper-labeled SDs are retained in their own units; Figure 4 on PDF p. 9 labels its error bars as standard errors of the mean, so the SD/SE conflict remains unresolved. No SE or confidence interval of the difference is printed. The model count in the PROCESS analysis is not applied to this separate t test. The mediation-model AI coefficient is excluded because that model adjusts for post-treatment interaction processes.

not_extracted.what: Cognitive diversity: AI access versus No AI access (earlier common baseline)
not_extracted.reason: The no-AI discussion occurred before AI access in every team; phase order was not randomized. It is neither an eligible randomized no-AI comparison nor an after_ai outcome (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2; PDF pp. 8–9, Section 4.2).

not_extracted.what: Task-quality balance test between future AI arms at baseline (Table 3)
not_extracted.reason: These submissions were produced before either randomized AI configuration was applied. This is a baseline balance comparison, not an effect with AI or after AI removal (PDF p. 10, Section 4.4.1; PDF p. 11, Table 3).

not_extracted.reason: These discussions precede AI exposure and test initial balance rather than an eligible with-AI or after-AI effect (PDF p. 10, Section 4.4.1; PDF p. 11, Table 3).

Originality is reported only as the dependent variable in a mediation analysis, with a mediator association and a serial indirect effect. No eligible total AI-arm contrast or arm means are printed; Figure 6 is a mediation-path diagram (PDF pp. 10–11, Section 4.4.2; PDF p. 12, Figure 6).

not_extracted.reason: These paths adjust for post-treatment team interaction processes. They are not total randomized effects of AI access and are excluded under the post-treatment-adjustment rule; the independent-sample contrast is retained separately (PDF pp. 8–10, Sections 4–4.3 and Figure 5; PDF p. 12, Figures 6–7).

open_items: The dispersions in Sections 4.1–4.2 (PDF pp. 8–9) are called SD, while Figure 4 says its error bars are standard errors of the mean. They are transcribed as printed SDs, but unambiguous SDs across randomized teams and confirmation of the labels are needed before standardization.

Table 1 (PDF p. 9) labels the adjacent statistic SD although it contains negative values and the footnote calls the entries t statistics. The record follows that footnote for the test field; no regression SE is supplied or reconstructed.

The study reports 120 participants, and Table 3 reports 40 unequal-access and 20 full-access teams at baseline. It does not separately label a final analyzed people total or print arm-level people counts and comparison-specific counts for the t tests. The study n_analyzed and all estimate-level people counts are therefore null. Team counts have not been multiplied into people counts, and model observation counts have not been relabeled as people.

OLS Table 1 reports 120 team-task observations, whereas the PROCESS model reports N = 60 (PDF pp. 8–9). The paper does not reconcile these model samples or specify how repeated teams across phases enter variance estimation. The OLS record lacks reported team-clustered precision.

The external supplement remains uninspected. The main article points to writing-task instructions, evaluation instructions/examples, and interaction coding in its Supplementary Sections 1–3 (PDF pp. 6–7 and 14). Retrieval attempts through the named Frontiers URL and DOI both failed with WinError 10013. Exact scoring aggregation, originality-score details, and any additional numerical results remain unconfirmed.
The release year of the paper-named Kimi 3.0 is not stated and remains null; the cited technical-report year does not confirm a release year for the named model.

The relationship to proceedings DOI 10.1002/pra2.1437 remains a deduplication issue: the screening form leaves overlap unconfirmed, and the citation record infers the same work but cannot confirm formal supersession. No participant-linkage statement appears in the journal PDF.
notes: Extracted on 2026-10-11 by extractor A from the supplied journal PDF. The complete markdown conversion was read in contiguous chunks through the final references; no appendix is appended. PDF pages cited here were extracted with pymupdf, and Tables 1 and 3 were also recovered with find_tables. Only the unequal-versus-full AI configuration comparison is randomized; the earlier no-AI phase is retained in the arm map for clarity but yields no eligible estimate. Baseline cluster counts are recorded as printed without converting them to people. Conservative analysis-specific count coding differs from the screening form, which carried the overall reported sample forward as analyzed. No numerical value was estimated from a figure or derived by calculation. All mediation-model effects are excluded, even where their dependent variable otherwise qualifies. The adjusted and unadjusted quality records are alternative analyses of the same outcome and sample. The quoted source text preserves the paper’s printed precision and signs. No supplement, dataset, or proceedings full text was used; the raw-data statement offers data from the authors but gives no public repository (PDF p. 14).
